## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Catutthapīṭhavimānavatthu* ("Fourth Throne Mansion", Vv 4) is a short poetic text situated within the *Vimānavatthu* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In the narrative, the Arahant Mahāmoggallāna encounters a *deva* and inquires about the specific meritorious actions that led to his rebirth in heaven and his possession of a divine throne composed of beryl gemstones [SuttaCentral].
While SuttaCentral lists no curated parallels in other languages or collections, it notes five translations across five modern languages [SuttaCentral]. Automatic text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates that the text shares 196 matching passages with 28 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest Pali reuse occurs with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (66 matches, including segments §4.2–7.4 aligned with §177–187 with 0.93 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial formulaic and verse overlap is also shared with closely related stories in the collection, particularly the other throne-themed poems—*Tatiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 3), *Paṭhamapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 1), and *Dutiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 2)—as well as the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10), and the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, DharmaNexus computes a machine alignment between segments of the Pali text (such as §1.2–1.4) and a Tibetan Kangyur text (BO_K01_D0007B-2_H0008-2) with a top score of 45 [DharmaNexus].
